groundRules.title: The 25-minute rule
groundRules.html: The 25-minute rule. Stuck for 25 minutes with zero progress → read the editorial → close it → re-solve from a blank file → add to Redo List. Staring for 2 hours is not grit, it is waste.

groundRules.title: Redo List is sacred
groundRules.html: Redo List is sacred. Every problem you could not solve unaided goes into a spreadsheet. Re-solve on Day+3, Day+10, Day+30. This single habit is worth ~40% of your final ability.

Java's Collections API is richer and its TreeMap gives you ordered-map operations that are genuinely nicer than C++'s. The two real costs: (1) verbosity — you type ~25% more, so practise typing speed and templates; (2) no lower_bound on arrays and no built-in pair/tuple — use int[]{a,b}, long encoding (a * 1_000_000L + b), or a small Pair class.
